findings.mechanism: SQL injection via string‑concatenated warehouse parameter
findings.remediation: Replace the concatenated query with a prepared statement using a placeholder for warehouse, e.g. `SELECT ... FROM items WHERE warehouse = $1` and pass the parameter to `pool.Query`
findings.arithmetic: None – the risk is logical, not numeric

findings.mechanism: Spawns an unbounded goroutine per SKU, creating one HTTP connection per goroutine and exhausting resources under load
findings.remediation: Introduce a bounded worker pool or semaphore to limit concurrent goroutines, e.g. limit to 20 concurrent pricing fetches

findings.mechanism: Pool max open connections set to 4, which is lower than typical worker count, causing request queuing and latency spikes
findings.remediation: Raise `SetMaxOpenConns` to match or exceed the number of HTTP workers (e.g. 16) or make it configurable

findings.mechanism: HTTP GET has no timeout, so a slow or hanging pricing service can block the request indefinitely
findings.remediation: Use a context with timeout (e.g. 5s) when performing the HTTP request and propagate the timeout to the caller
findings.arithmetic: Without timeout the request can wait the full latency of the pricing service; with a 30 s latency the observed latency is ≥30 000 ms

findings.mechanism: Per‑item `Reserved` query causes N+1 database queries, scaling linearly with item count and increasing load
findings.remediation: Rewrite the handler to fetch reservations in bulk (e.g. join or IN clause) so only a constant number of queries are issued per request
